# Exact reflected-pair depth superlevels need not be convex, even at the OC level

This note tests one precise arithmetic gluing step. At each actual integer anchor, retain its own fiber and **every complete reflected pair**, with their full original measures and all ambient cap directions. Even the exact best depth of this retained source need not have convex, or same-parity-midpoint-closed, superlevels as the anchor varies. The failure occurs at the actual OC threshold on a complete convex mixed-integer body with equal fibers. It does not refute OC or every possible use of Helly's theorem.

The archive already establishes different failures: `candidate 8a1fb011e3d0549f` shows that ordinary-depth allocation hulls can be empty, while `candidate 325d279c18e3a49e` disproves an own-depth capacity lower bound. Here no ordinary-depth approximation is made within a reflected pair: its entire actual halfspace contribution is retained. The information discarded is only the unpaired fibers, and the resulting source changes with the integer anchor.

## 1. Exact reflected sources

Let Q be a full-dimensional bounded lattice polytope in R^n and P=Q intersect Z^n. Let F be a full-dimensional convex body of volume v in R^d, d>=1, and use the actual product body C=Q times F. For p in P define

    P[p]={z in P:2p-z in P},
    S[p]=P[p] times F,
    D_p(x)=inf_{H closed ambient halfspace, (p,x) in H} mu(S[p] intersect H),
    A_p=sup_{x in F} D_p(x).

The base P[p] is exactly (Q intersect (2p-Q)) intersect Z^n, so its integer fibers come from an actual reflected convex intersection. That intersection may have lower integer affine dimension at a boundary anchor, which does not affect the retained fiber measure. It includes the own base p and every distinct reflected pair about p. Its counting size N_p is odd. Measures are ordinary d-volume summed over the retained bases; no volume is renormalized.

For the unit interval F=[-1/2,1/2],

    A_p=N_p/2.                                           (1)

Indeed S[p] is centrally symmetric about (p,0). Every closed halfspace containing that point has at least half its total measure, by pairing points under reflection; positive boundary mass can only increase the count. The continuous-coordinate cut x>=0 has exactly half. At any other x, the containing horizontal upper or lower cap on the shorter side has measure N_p(1/2-|x|)<=N_p/2. Thus (1) is an exact maximized depth, not just a lower certificate.

More generally, if F is a d-simplex of volume v and Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d, the previously proved ordinary paired-centroid-tail theorem gives

    A_p=N_p Gamma_d v.                                  (2)

For completeness, its application is exact. Let g be the centroid of F. A nonvertical through-(p,g) ambient cap restricts to opposite scalar threshold shifts on each reflected base pair. The theorem in `candidate 732b11a769399016` gives at least 2Gamma_d v per pair and ordinary Grünbaum gives Gamma_d v on the own fiber. A purely integer cap through p contains the own fiber and at least one member of every pair, hence at least (N_p+1)v/2>=N_p Gamma_d v. Translate a containing boundary through (p,g) if necessary.

Conversely, the d+1 canonical centroid vertex caps of a simplex cover F and each has volume Gamma_d v. Extend them horizontally across all retained integer bases. Every point (p,x) lies in one such cap, of mass N_p Gamma_d v. This proves the upper bound for every x and (2); the supremum is attained at the single deterministic point g. The d=1 instance is the elementary argument (1), independent of that auxiliary theorem.

## 2. Nine complete integer bases with a 5,3,5 reflected pattern

Take the actual planar pentagon

    Q_0=conv{(-3,0),(-1,-1),(0,-1),(3,1),(2,1)}.

An exact halfspace description is

    y>=-1,  y<=1,
    x+2y>=-3,  2x-3y<=3,  x-5y>=-3.

Thus its complete integer set is

    P_0={(-1,-1),(0,-1)}
          union {(-3,0),(-2,0),(-1,0),(0,0),(1,0)}
          union {(2,1),(3,1)}.                         (3)

The row description follows by substituting the only possible integer y values -1,0,1 into the displayed inequalities. All nine points, and no omitted lattice points, are present.

For anchors p_-=(-1,0), p_0=(0,0), p_+=(1,0), direct reflection gives

    P_0[p_-]={(-3,0),(-2,0),(-1,0),(0,0),(1,0)},
    P_0[p_0]={(-1,0),(0,0),(1,0)},
    P_0[p_+]={(-1,-1),(0,-1),(1,0),(2,1),(3,1)}.        (4)

In particular their exact reflected-source maxima are 5Gamma_d v, 3Gamma_d v, and 5Gamma_d v for simplex fibers. At level 4Gamma_d v the two outer anchors qualify and their integer midpoint does not. The two outer anchors have the same integer parity.

Therefore this depth-superlevel base set is not the trace on P_0 of any convex set in R^2. Nor can the corresponding full local candidate region be the trace of a convex set in the ambient space: it contains (p_-,g) and (p_+,g), but not their midpoint. In fact no point in the entire midpoint fiber qualifies.

This example already retains identical own fibers, joint concavity of the ordinary own-depth root, exact reflected pair geometry, and optimization over the continuous source point. None of those properties supplies the missing convexity.

## 3. The same failure at the original OC target

To place the nonconvexity exactly at the task's target, add one genuine binary integer layer, rather than altering any measure weights. Put

    Q_1=[0,4]^2,
    Q=conv((Q_0 times {0}) union (Q_1 times {1})) subset R^3.

This is a compact full-dimensional convex polytope. The only integer values of its last coordinate are 0 and 1. Its exact end sections are Q_0 and Q_1. Consequently its complete integer base is

    P=(P_0 times {0}) union ({0,1,2,3,4}^2 times {1}),
    |P|=9+25=34.                                      (5)

Use C=Q times F with a d-simplex F of volume v. This is a full-dimensional convex body in R^(3+d); every integer fiber has positive full d-volume v and M=34v. The OC raw target is

    r=2^(-3) Gamma_d M=(17/4)Gamma_d v.               (6)

At an anchor in layer 0, both members of a reflected pair must stay in layer 0, since their last coordinates lie in {0,1} and sum to zero. Thus the reflected sources at (p_-,0), (p_0,0), and (p_+,0) are unchanged from (4). Their maxima are respectively

    5Gamma_d v > r,
    3Gamma_d v < r,
    5Gamma_d v > r.                                   (7)

The two qualifying anchors still have the same parity and their integer midpoint is the nonqualifying anchor. All eight parities are occupied in P, so this also uses the full occupied-parity budget, not an artificially loose rank bound.

For every n>3, take [0,1]^(n-3) times this body. Within any fixed binary block, reflected pairs remain in that block. The total mass is multiplied by 2^(n-3), exactly canceled by the OC factor 2^(-n), so (6)--(7) persist in every integer rank n>=3 and every continuous dimension d>=1.

## 4. What fails in a parity-Helly assembly

The finite occupied-parity Helly theorem applies to convex sets and their traces on a midpoint-closed lattice base. Sections 2--3 prove that the natural superlevel trace

    {p in P : there exists x in F with D_p(x)>=r}

does not satisfy that necessary trace property. There is no convex set with exactly this trace: convexity would include the integer midpoint of the two displayed outer anchors. Taking its convex hull would introduce an anchor at which the retained-pair conclusion is rigorously false for every continuous source.

Accordingly one cannot apply occupied-parity Helly directly to these varying-anchor exact reflected-depth superlevels, or assert their convexity from joint ordinary own-depth-root concavity. Fixed-measure depth regions are convex; here the retained measure itself depends on p. This distinction is the precise obstruction. The note does not exclude a different construction that retains common normals, unpaired credit, a fixed measure, or additional joint incidence data.

## 5. Independent safety calibration

The full example has an explicit good point. In its layer 1 take integer base (2,2,1) and continuous coordinate g. Its complete reflected source is the entire 5 by 5 upper layer, because that square lattice set is centrally symmetric about (2,2). Formula (2) gives raw depth at least 25Gamma_d v for the retained upper layer, hence also for the original source. This strictly exceeds the target (17/4)Gamma_d v. For d=1 the assertion follows just by central symmetry, with no external geometric inequality. Additional binary blocks only add mass.

Thus the construction is an OC-safe actual body and an exact obstruction only to the stated convexity/Helly step. No numerical optimization, missing-fiber approximation, or selected-center limit is used in the certificate.
